description: Customer relationship platform and CRM for contact management, deals, sales activity, pipeline management, and related customer data.
self_serve_details: A free CRM account can be created without a credit card and has no expiration. API credentials are account-scoped: creating legacy private apps requires super-admin access; app scopes and rate limits depend on account entitlements and subscription. Public/multi-account applications use OAuth.

credential_access.path: For a single-account integration, a HubSpot super admin creates a scoped private app and copies its Bearer access token in the account. For a public/multi-account app, register/configure an app on the developer platform and use OAuth.
credential_access.plan_or_gate: Account and permission required; private-app creation is super-admin-only. API quotas and available scopes vary by subscription and API feature. Free CRM availability does not prove every scope or feature is free.

api.details: REST APIs cover CRM objects and related records; webhooks are supported. Private-app documentation shows configurable scopes and object-event subscriptions. Some API areas and limits depend on account entitlements; CMS GraphQL is not treated as general CRM API breadth.

mcp.details: HubSpot documents a remote CRM MCP server for secure, scoped read/write access and a separate local Developer MCP server. Remote setup uses the current developer platform and OAuth credentials; accessible objects/tools depend on configured app scopes and server capabilities.
mcp.search_scope: Opened HubSpot's first-party MCP overview and private-app/developer-platform docs; first-party documentation directly lists both MCP servers and remote CRM setup.

buildability.blocker: Account-specific scopes, super-admin setup for private tokens, and plan-dependent features/quotas; public OAuth apps require developer-platform app configuration.
buildability.rationale: Broad documented CRM REST APIs and an official MCP option support a feasible connector, but production access must respect account scopes, permissions, distribution, and subscription entitlements.

api.details: Official REST API supports reading/writing workspace data, with endpoint coverage for records, objects, lists, and related activities; webhooks and an App SDK are part of the developer platform. MCP additionally supports broad workspace read/write operations.

mcp.search_scope: Opened Attio's own developer overview, REST auth guide, MCP overview, help-center token guide, and pricing page; MCP ownership and URL are explicit in official docs.

buildability.blocker: A workspace admin must issue API keys; OAuth/MCP operations are limited to the authorizing user's workspace permissions and scopes.
buildability.rationale: Public REST, webhook, and MCP surfaces plus a free plan make a connector feasible, but credentials and data access remain workspace-admin/user-permission scoped.

buildability.blocker: Base rate limits; elevated throughput and some programmatic app-token or high-trust operations require add-on or support interaction.

self_serve_details: Copper offers a self-serve trial; API keys are generated from the Copper web app by an admin and used with the owner email. OAuth 2.0 is the preferred route for partner integrations, but official OAuth quickstart says the application must be registered and client credentials obtained by contacting Copper. Current API entitlement by plan was not resolved from the opened pricing matrix.

credential_access.path: For single-user/internal use, an admin generates an API key in System Settings > API Keys and supplies the token-owner email. For a partner integration, register the app and obtain OAuth client ID/secret through Copper's partner channel.
credential_access.plan_or_gate: Admin/account access required for a user API key; partner OAuth app registration requires contact with partners@copper.com. The official pricing page did not expose which plan includes API entitlement in the opened text.

api.details: Copper's official Developer API is a REST/JSON interface for most Copper resources, using API-key headers or OAuth. Detailed resource coverage includes core CRM entities, but this assessment does not infer unlisted APIs or count endpoints; plan entitlement remains unresolved.

mcp.details: No first-party Copper MCP documentation was identified in the official developer or product pages opened. Third-party wrappers surfaced in discovery but do not establish Copper ownership; status remains UNKNOWN rather than a categorical absence claim.
mcp.search_scope: Opened Copper's developer/API documentation, API-key and OAuth guides, pricing page, and targeted official-domain MCP searches; no official MCP page/repository was verified, and no exhaustive first-party repo/catalog audit was completed.

buildability.blocker: Account-admin API-key setup, partner contact for OAuth client credentials, and unresolved plan-level API entitlement.
buildability.rationale: A documented REST API and token/OAuth paths support integration, but multi-tenant app registration and which Copper subscription unlocks API use require confirmation before promising an unrestricted connector.

description: Deal and relationship intelligence platform for professional firms, including pipeline, contact, firm, and investment/deal management.
self_serve_details: DealCloud API access is tenant-specific. An organization administrator must enable the API capability for the user's group; the user then enables/copies an API key in their profile. API documentation directs users without admin access to their organization's administrator or DealCloud Customer Success Manager. First-party MCP additionally requires DealCloud with Celeste licensing and admin/user MCP permissions.

credential_access.path: Use an existing DealCloud tenant, have its admin grant API capability to the user's group, enable/copy the profile API key, then exchange the client ID/key for a short-lived OAuth2 bearer token with required scopes.
credential_access.plan_or_gate: Existing tenant plus administrator-enabled API capability and group permissions; MCP requires a DealCloud with Celeste license, Manage MCP Servers for admins, and MCP Access for end users. No self-serve trial/standalone developer account path was confirmed.

api.details: Official REST APIs cover structured data CRUD, schema/metadata, user management, backups, publications/real-time events, and relationship intelligence. Access is site- and permission-scoped; OAuth2 client credentials yield bearer tokens.

mcp.details: DealCloud's first-party default MCP server is available at a tenant-specific URL. It exposes site schema/context to compatible AI clients; usage requires DealCloud with Celeste licensing, administrator server-management permission, and end-user MCP Access.
mcp.search_scope: Opened first-party DealCloud MCP overview and Getting Started, API overview, OAuth token/API-key docs, data API docs, and official product page; licensing and permissions are specified in the MCP guide.

buildability.blocker: Requires a provisioned customer tenant and system-admin/API capability; MCP use additionally requires the Celeste license and MCP permissions.
buildability.rationale: DealCloud has broad REST APIs and an official MCP server, but both are customer-tenant/permission dependent; this is feasible within an authorized client account, not a public self-serve connector test.
